result.reason: 4 findings, 3 of them important, and 2 dropped.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: drivingResult warns when a day drives no longer than the comfortable hours but longer than an approval that gives fewer hours. No test checks this. The only driving tests use a day that is already over the comfortable hours (Day 5 with no approval, and Day 4 at 4 h 18 m against 4 comfortable hours).
findings.failure_case: Change the guard to `if (!isOver) return null`. A day with 3 h of driving, 4 comfortable hours and a 2-hour approval then gives no warning, and every test still passes.
findings.label_reason: The change adds this rule, and no test fails if it is deleted, so F6 fits. None of the labels above it fit because the code itself works.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: misfitOf warns about a nearEndPlace stop that is no longer on the last day. No test checks this. The search area test only covers a nearStay stop and a nearStartPlace stop.
findings.failure_case: Delete the nearEndPlace branch. A 'pie' stop near the end place, moved to Day 2, then gets no searchAreaDoesNotFitDay warning, and every test still passes.
findings.label_reason: The change adds this behavior, and no test would fail without it, so F6 fits. The code works, so no fix label above F6 applies.

findings.label: F6
findings.problem: openingHoursText says '<place> opens at <time>' when the place opens during the visit, using openingChangeWithin. No test reaches the 'opens' case. Milt's only checks 'closes', and no test calls openingChangeWithin directly.
findings.failure_case: Make openingChangeWithin return only closings. A visit from 10:30 a.m. at a place that opens at 11:00 a.m. then gets the 'open for only ...' text instead of 'opens at 11:00 a.m.', and every test still passes.
findings.label_reason: The change adds this text path and the 'opens' change, and no test checks them, so F6 fits. Nothing is shown to be wrong in the code, so no label above it fits.

findings.label: NF1
findings.problem: openingChangeWithin treats every span edge as an opening or a closing, even where one period closes at the same minute the next one opens. At that minute the place stays open, but the function reports 'closes' there. The warning text then names a closing time that isn't real.
findings.failure_case: Take periods Monday 11:00–14:00 and 14:00–16:00, and a visit from 13:00 to 17:00. A run gives 180 open minutes and {change: 'closes', minute: 840}. So the warning says the place 'closes at 2:00 p.m.', but it really closes at 4:00 p.m.
findings.label_reason: This is new code, and the run shows the wrong result. Google seldom returns periods that touch like this, and a visit has to cover the join and also run past a real closing, so this isn't normal use. That makes it NF1, which is a nit because the change added it.

dropped.problem: The daily driving text 'You agreed to 5.' leaves out the unit, so it could be unclear to the coordinator agent.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: The domain model's CheckResult text example at design/domain-model.md line 471 gives this exact wording. Its sentence before it already says 'needs about 4 h 18 m of driving', so the text is not false.

dropped.problem: stopOrderResult compares leg.stopsInBestOrder with day.stops by object identity. A leg loaded from storage might hold different Stop objects, so the order would never match.
dropped.label: D1
dropped.reason: legFromStored in src/domain/stored-itinerary.ts maps stopIdsInBestOrder through stopOf, which returns the itinerary's own Stop objects. LegsService builds the order from route.stops, the day's own selected stops. So the identity check compares the same objects.
